meta_description: One governed decision API with replay outperforms a zoo of embedded models.

blocks.x: One governed decision API with replay outperforms a zoo of embedded models.

The argument for Decision hubs beat model sprawl is simple: decisions made on stale information cost more than the platform that would make them current — and the gap is measurable in weeks, not years.

items: Separability (models score, policy decides, humans supervise) survives audit and staff turnover.
Champion-challenger discipline makes model risk a measured, improving quantity.
Decision replay converts regulatory questions from expeditions into queries.

blocks.x: Three questions to ask your current vendors

items: Ask for the baseline: how was the starting position measured, and who signed it?
Ask for the trail: can your auditors replay any decision the system made last week, end to end?
Ask for the unit cost: what does one decision cost to run, and who owns keeping it down?

blocks.x: Programs like Decision hubs beat model sprawl rarely fail on the technology. They fail on unnamed ownership, unmeasured baselines and ungated scope — the three failure modes the guards on this page are built for.

items: Every stage has a gate with real stop authority — scope expands on measured deltas, not on momentum.
The operating model is designed first — who decides what, at which gate, holding which evidence.
Evidence is generated while the work happens, so the audit is a walkthrough, not an archaeology project.

blocks.x: P99 decision latency under 150 ms is a production standard, not an aspiration.
